variables.claim_asserts: At Darwin's present day, few European productions had become naturalised in Australia or La Plata, while many La Plata productions had become naturalised in Australia.
variables.test_measures: Counts and asymmetry of vascular-plant native and introduced distributions in the 2026 World Checklist of Vascular Plants for Europe, Australia, and La Plata.

modality.note: WCVP is suitable for modern vascular-plant distributions, but modern introduced ranges include roughly 167 additional years of trade and naturalisation after the historical observation.

assumptions.note: The analysis treats present-day modern naturalisations as if they could refute Darwin's explicitly contemporaneous 1859 distribution pattern.

scope.claim_scope: The naturalisation pattern existing at Darwin's present day, across the productions he discussed.
scope.test_scope: Modern WCVP vascular-plant distributions and current introduced status in three operationalized regions.

reasons: The claim's temporal variable is the distribution observed in 1859, whereas the dataset records modern distributions in 2026.
Post-1859 introductions and naturalisations can reverse the historical asymmetry without showing Darwin's contemporary observation was false.
The result itself acknowledges that it tests the present-day pattern rather than Darwin's 1859 reading, and it further narrows productions to vascular plants.
what_would_change_it: Use contemporaneous circa-1859 floras and faunas for Europe, La Plata, and Australia, applying comparable historical native and naturalised-status definitions.
